Week of 2026-09-03

Exponential View
Host: Azeem Azhar, with Greg Williams (ex-WIRED UK editor-in-chief, joined as Executive Editor in April 2026) increasingly co-hosting
Why for Fred: His AI list (Dwarkesh, MLST, No Priors, Latent Space, Me Myself and AI, The Cognitive Revolution, Training Data, The AI Daily Brief) is now unusually deep but skews toward researchers, engineers, VCs, and operators -- none approach AI from Azhar's economist/policy lens, tracking exponential technological change and its institutional and labour-market effects at a societal level. Azhar's own writing (the book Exponential Age, his weekly essays) is the closest match to the "AI impact on work" thread in Fred's profile, distinct from the capital-allocation or engineering registers already covered.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: "Are We in Charge of Our AI Tools... or Are They in Charge of Us?" (Feb 25, 2026, with Nita Farahany and Eric Topol)
Link: https://www.exponentialview.co/listen

The Matt Walker Podcast
Host: Dr. Matthew Walker (UC Berkeley neuroscientist, author of Why We Sleep)
Why for Fred: The health list is heavy on longevity and dementia prevention (The Peter Attia Drive, Health Longevity Secrets, Dementia Matters, FoundMyFitness, The Genius Life, all previously suggested) and breathwork (Oxygen Advantage), but sleep -- one of the most evidence-backed levers for cognitive and metabolic health in the ~50 cohort, and directly upstream of dementia risk -- hasn't had a dedicated show yet. Walker is the field's leading public voice, and the show translates primary sleep-research literature into specific protocols the same way Attia and FoundMyFitness do for their own domains.
Format: Long-form deep-dive, roughly twice monthly, 60-90+ min
Sample episode: "Debunking 11 Sleep Myths" (Aug 31, 2026)
Link: https://themattwalkerpodcast.buzzsprout.com/

Sound School Podcast
Host: Rob Rosenthal (Transom/PRX)
Why for Fred: Scriptnotes and Writing Excuses (both previously suggested) cover fiction and screenwriting craft in prose and dialogue terms, but neither touches audio production itself -- the actual medium behind Lightfin. Rosenthal interviews working radio producers and documentarians about sound design, tape editing, interview technique, and pacing for the ear specifically, which is the more directly applicable craft skill for ongoing children's-audio production than any prose-focused writing show already on the list.
Format: Short craft-focused interview/teardown, biweekly, ~20-30 min
Sample episode: Andrew Leland episode on his Radiolab reporting trip (~May 5, 2026)
Link: https://transom.org/topics/soundschool/

Circles Off
Host: Rob Pizzola, with the "Circle Back" segment co-hosted by Jacob Gramegna and Geoff Fienberg
Why for Fred: The Unabated Podcast and Sharp Football Analysis (both previously suggested) cover sports betting from the NFL-model and matchup-analytics angle, largely through Rufus Peabody's orbit; Circles Off is a different voice entirely -- Pizzola runs a platform-and-strategy-focused show covering line shopping, book limiting, prediction markets, and the business side of being a professional bettor. A genuinely distinct angle on the same sports-betting domain rather than more of the same modeling talk.
Format: Interview/roundtable, semiweekly, ~13 min-2 hr
Sample episode: "I Asked the Co-Founder of Our Sponsor the Hard Questions" (Aug 26, 2026)
Link: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/circles-off-sports-betting-podcasts/id1552575702

Week of 2026-08-27

The Investor's Podcast (formerly We Study Billionaires)
Host: Stig Brodersen, William Green, Shawn O'Malley, Daniel Mahncke, Kyle Grieve
Why for Fred: The direct, dedicated home for Buffett/Berkshire principles that his current lineup only touches in passing -- recent completed episodes on Diary of a CEO (Ray Dalio) and Invest Like the Best show he's actively pulling on this thread. Where Invest Like the Best ranges across all of investing, this show is narrower and deeper: dissecting individual Buffett/Munger/Dalio/Howard Marks letters and case studies, with William Green (author of Richer, Wiser, Happier) bringing the same "study the masters" lens Fred already applies via Business Breakdown-style teardown analysis.
Format: Long-form interview + solo teaching episodes, 2-3x/week, ~45-75 min
Sample episode: Any recent episode breaking down a Buffett shareholder letter or a Howard Marks memo -- check the feed for the latest
Link: https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/the-investors-podcast-show/

Yet Another Value Podcast
Host: Andrew Walker
Why for Fred: World of Short Selling (suggested previously) covers the short side; this is the long-side complement for the same event-driven, special-situations niche that Pender Fund and Behind the Balance Sheet gesture at but don't centre -- busted compounders, spin-offs, weird capital structures, and activist situations, pitched by the fund managers actually holding the position. Recent 2026 episodes (Alex Roepers of Atlantic Investment Management on Dauch and Nomad Foods; Pershing Square Challenge pitches) are exactly the kind of concrete, numbers-first idea generation the MOI Global-adjacent thread of the wiki already favours.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~60-90 min
Sample episode: The Alex Roepers episode on Dauch (DCH) and Nomad Foods (NOMD) -- two live deep-value special situations argued in detail
Link: https://www.yetanothervalueblog.com/s/yet-another-value-podcast

The Genius Life
Host: Max Lugavere
Why for Fred: The Peter Attia Drive, Health Longevity Secrets, Dementia Matters, and FoundMyFitness (all previously suggested) approach dementia prevention from the physician/researcher side; Lugavere comes at the identical territory from a science-journalist-turned-advocate angle, driven by his own mother's dementia diagnosis, making the material more narrative and practically actionable rather than purely clinical. A February 2026 brain-health AMA covers dementia prevention, memory, and supplement protocols directly.
Format: Long-form interview + solo Q&A, weekly, ~60-90 min
Sample episode: "The Alzheimer's Fraud That Derailed Research for Decades" (Ep. 244, with Matt Bilinsky)
Link: https://www.maxlugavere.com/podcast/244

The AI Daily Brief
Host: Nathaniel Whittemore (NLW)
Why for Fred: The Cognitive Revolution (previously suggested) already fills part of the "staying current" gap, but at biweekly ~60-90 min episodes it can't match model-release velocity; AI Daily Brief runs near-daily at ~20 minutes, functioning as a running news ticker across inference economics, enterprise AI adoption, and startup funding -- the same threads spread across Fred's more analytical AI shows (Dwarkesh, No Priors, Latent Space, Me Myself and AI), compressed into a briefing rather than a deep-dive commitment.
Format: News/analysis briefing, near-daily cadence, ~20 min
Sample episode: Any recent episode reacting to a frontier model release or major AI funding round
Link: https://aidailybrief.ai/
